text: Dreaming 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的技能能力跟踪插件。它接入技能调用、工具结果与会话事件，先预测技能对当前任务的适配情况，再比较预期和实际表现，形成技能级的能力记录。插件会把历史边界提示注入系统提示词，并在技能结果后附上简短说明；定时校准流程可根据表现差异生成技能描述或边界调整。设置面板展示调用记录、判定、趋势与梦境日志，也提供手动运行和回滚入口。预测与判定使用当前 DSH 配置的模型服务。

Dreaming evaluates DSH skill use: it predicts fit, records outcomes, and judges results. It injects learned boundaries into prompts and reviews mismatches to propose description edits. A web panel displays skill history with run and revert controls. It uses DSH’s configured model provider.
想知道某个技能对当前任务是否真的适用。
希望根据实际调用结果改进技能描述和能力边界。
I want to compare a skill’s predicted usefulness with what happened after it ran.
Dreaming 的功能「技能效果评估」：技能加载时并行预测它对当前任务的适配度，回合结束后结合观察到的结果进行判定，并记录每个技能的表现。
Dreaming 的功能「技能边界校准」：定时筛选表现不佳或存在能力差距的技能案例，调用梦境流程形成描述或边界调整，并通过设置面板查看记录与管理修改。
Dreaming 会把技能任务及截断后的调用轨迹用于模型探测和判定，使用当前配置的模型服务处理这些内容。

> Knowing what a skill can actually do *before* you execute it — that is **consciousness strength**. Dreaming raises it by measuring every skill call and correcting skill boundaries overnight, so skills are invoked precisely and tokens are not wasted on descriptions that merely *look* right.

Dreaming is a global DeepSeek Harness plugin (Host plugin + Web panel). It is not a logging plugin; it is a **capability self-model**:

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · Why it exists：Dreaming closes the loop: **measure → judge → write the boundary back → measure again**. The metric is rising consciousness and falling wasted tokens, not the number of log lines.

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · How it works：```
                    ┌──────────── every skill call ────────────┐
user/agent ── skill ─┤ tools/pre-execute                        │
                    │   ├─ record the task context (truncated)  │
                    │   └─ concurrent probe: a cheap LLM call   │

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · 1. Probe — predict at load time, in parallel：Inside `tools/pre-execute` the plugin registers an episode before the skill runs and starts a budgeted prediction subtask concurrently (default `probe.mode = 'subagent'`, a real caller-delivered child via `ctx.subagents.startActivation({ delivery: 'caller' })`; `inline` uses `ctx.llm.stream` directly). The probe returns a structured prediction:
section: 1. Probe — predict at load time, in parallel
1. Probe — predict at load time, in parallel

text:
dsh-plugin-dreaming README · 1. Probe — predict at load time, in parallel：> Subagents are the default: both prediction and judgement run as caller-delivered subtasks, and the skill call never waits for them (`probe.attachDeadlineMs` defaults to 0). If the service is unavailable, times out, or returns no text, the plugin falls back to a single inline call, so behaviour never disappears. `inline` is cheaper for cost-sensitive setups.
>
> The task pack only takes real user requests: user-role metadata such as `runtime-context`, AGENTS instructions and `<system-reminder>` is filtered out, and the whole derivation is scanned — otherwise “Time sampled…” can masquerade as the task.
section: 1. Probe — predict at load time, in parallel

text: dsh-plugin-dreaming README · 2. Observe the real outcome：`tools/result` records the skill load; `session/event` collects a bounded trace from the load point: assistant text, tool-call sequence (name/outcome/summary), user corrections, and the `turn/end` reason. The window closes at the same turn's `turn/end`, or after `observe.maxTurnExtensionMs` / `observe.maxEvents`. Closed sessions are never read again and the window does not stay in memory.
dsh-plugin-dreaming README · 3. Judge — expectation vs reality：After the turn, one judge call produces (default `judge.mode = 'subagent'`, also a caller-delivered child; falls back to inline):
dsh-plugin-dreaming README · 4. Capability belief and consciousness：Each skill keeps a belief: load count, verdict distribution, fit history, cost, learned boundaries. Core metrics:

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · 4. Capability belief and consciousness：| Metric | Definition | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `fitAccuracy` | `1 − Brier score` (predicted fit vs. actual success) | Does it predict *itself* accurately? |
| `boundaryAccuracy` | `1 − share of judged calls with a capability gap` | Is its stated boundary accurate? |
| `precision` | `1 − misapplied / judged` (judged calls only) | When it was called, was it on topic? |
| `consciousness` | `100 × (0.45·fitAccuracy + 0.30·boundaryAccuracy + 0.25·precision)` | The combined consciousness score |
| `wasteRate` | wasted tokens / loaded skill tokens | How much did it waste? |
| `confidence` | `<3 / <10 / ≥10 judged` → low / medium / high | How trustworthy is the score? |

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · 4. Capability belief and consciousness：> No fake high score with few samples: `confidence = low` is reported, and both the panel and the model-facing text say so.
>
> Waste accounting: a call judged `misapplied` or `missed` counts its whole skill-body cost as wasted; `partial` only counts rework tokens when rework was actually observed.

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · Install：Requires DSH ≥ 0.2.1-0 (see `engines.dsh`).

Install from this Git repository (the plugin is distributed from GitHub; npm publishing is planned).

In the Harness **Plugins** page, paste the repository URL:

```
https://github.com/puppetcat-fire/dsh-plugin-dreaming
```

or from the CLI for a profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add git+https://github.com/puppetcat-fire/dsh-plugin-dreaming.git
```

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · Install：A profile-level bundle takes effect for all sessions and survives restarts. Remove it from the Plugins page, or with `plugin_manager(action="remove_bundle", target="dsh-plugin-dreaming")`.

> Runtime packages (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis`) are provided by Harness; they are declared as `peerDependencies` and need no separate install.

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · Configuration：All configuration lives in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (or a home patch). The plugin exports no editable volatile fields, so Settings shows no generic form; Settings → Dreaming is a read-only observability page. Defaults are defined in `lib/config.js`. The most useful keys:

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch |
| `dataDir` | `''` | Data directory; empty = `$DSH_HOME/dreaming` |
| `probe.enabled` | `true` | Predict on skill load |
| `probe.mode` | `'subagent'` | `subagent` (default, real child) or `inline` (cheaper, used as the fallback) |
| `probe.sampleRate` | `1` | Sampling rate; known-gap skills are always probed |
| `probe.reasoningEffort` | `'low'` | `off` / `low` / `high` / `max`; empty inherits the session route (DeepSeek rejects `medium`) |
| `probe.attachDeadlineMs` | `0` | Max wait for the same-call prediction; 0 (default) never blocks the skill call, and the prediction is still recorded for the judge |
| `probe.maxPerHour` | `120` | Hourly probe cap |
| `judge.enabled` | `true` | Judge after the turn |
| `judge.mode` | `'subagent'` | `subagent` (default) or `inline`; falls back automatically |
| `judge.reasoningEffort` | `'low'` | `off` / `low` / `high` / `max`; empty inherits |
| `observe.maxTurnExtensionMs` | `600000` | Hard cap on the observation window |
| `prompt.awarenessSection` | `true` | Inject the global awareness section |

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · Panel：The panel only reads `/dreaming/api/*` (a Host prefix route: JSON only, Origin check on POST, request-size limit). Every write goes through the same revert path as the dream engine.

dsh-plugin-dreaming README · Known limitations：- **No edits by default**: `dream.autoApply` is `false`, so dreams journal proposals without touching files. Enable it explicitly to correct descriptions/boundaries (backups, journal, conflict detection and revert still apply).
- **Suggestions need samples**: the first calls of a new skill show only low-confidence hints; the plugin deliberately never fabricates a high score without evidence.
- **Non-editable sources**: bundled / project / runtime skills can only improve through the injected guidance overlay; their files are never rewritten.
- **Capability edits are heuristic**: dream proposals pass deterministic validation, but a “better description” can still introduce bias; that is why backups, journal, conflict detection and single-step revert exist.
- **Dream is inline-only in v1**: the night usually has no live parent agent; `dream.mode` is recorded truthfully as `inline` and logs one warning.
- **Symlinks are not edited**: if a skill's `SKILL.md` is a symlink the plugin refuses to write (`symlink-path`) and only records a suggestion, so the link is never replaced by a regular file.
